src: A Miner mines iron veins in mines (pay, threaten or persuade the foreman) and one-off deposits on hillsides and fields: 7–10 per node.
Dropped by enemies and found in containers.
Small amounts from dismantling gear at the Workshop.
Iron Ore.q: Iron ore can be used to make weapons, armor and building components.

src: Chopping blocks at sawmills, logging camps, farms and bandit camps (9–12 each; anyone with an axe can chop, Woodcutters get more), e.g. Lund Farm and Stromkapp Mill in Tiltren, plus random tree stumps.
Some quests reward Wood (e.g. Missing Woodcutters: 20).
Wood.q: The quintessential fuel source, wood is also useful for making boats and weapon handles.

src: The Tanning Rack turns animal carcasses into Leather during rest.
Marketplace traders and some general merchants.
Leather.q: This leather is used to craft weapons, armour and armour layering.

src: A Tier 2 Tanning Rack turns Ghost Carcasses (from Ghost Packs in foggy forests at night) into White Leather. The Tier 2 blueprint costs 200 Pristine Fangs at the Trackers Camp (County of Arthes).
Rare: some Trackers Camps and specialised merchants.
White Leather.q: An odd type of leather, which is exeptionally tough despite its silky texture.

src: An upgraded Campfire burns up to 10 Wood into 10 Coal each rest.
Blacksmith merchants (e.g. Master Hulan and Claes in Tiltren) and some marketplace traders.
Coal.q: Coal can be used with iron to forge powerful weapons and armour.

src: Dropped by humanoid enemies (refugees, plague victims, bandits) and found in containers.
Helmets and hoods at the Workshop have a high chance to give Cloth.
The Drapery (Vertruse), Shabby Camp (Arthes), Marheim Market, town blacksmiths and roaming merchants.
Cloth.q: This cloth fabric allows you to craft clothing that will stand the test of time.

src: A Tinkerer makes it at the Workshop from Hemp (picked at farms; starting recipe).
Tiltren Prison refills every few days.
Rope.q: The hemp rope is used to make bows as well as gear for navigation and climbing. In a pinch, it can also be used to tie up a captured animal.

src: An Experienced Alchemist makes it from Grey Clusters (Experienced Miner, or Gold Caravan merchants) and Alazarian Powder (Alchemist byproduct). The recipe costs 1 Knowledge Point.
Journeyman Miners can find Rimesteel ore (northwest Grinmeer coast, mountains near Gosenberg).
Limited stock at Gosenberg Apothecary, Grinmeer Apothecary Clinic (Femetruda), lit-wagon traveling merchants (up to 5) and Gold Caravan merchants.
Rimesteel.q: Rimesteel is a recently discovered metal that doesn't occur naturally and is very difficult to extract. Only the best blacksmiths can make use of it.

src: A Journeyman Alchemist makes it from Etherite (Journeyman Miner) and Alchemical Residue (Journeyman Alchemist byproduct).
Belerion blacksmiths sell Akhedian ingots (Pirates of Belerion DLC).
Akhedian Steel.q: Akhedian steel is named after the city of Akhed in Ihraa. Without the help of their scholars, the Five Kingdoms would never have discovered how to use etherite.

src: A Master Alchemist makes it from Carmine Tanbark, gathered by a skilled Woodcutter (e.g. the chopping spots at Rouste Field on Tule Island, Belerion).
Vairmeil.q: Those who know how to craft vairmeil are careful not to share their knowledge: this extraordinary material is so highly prized that selling it is enough to ensure their family's fortune.

src: From the creatures of The Beast Hunt DLC.
Bone of the Beast.q: The toughness of this bone isn't the only obstacle to making weapons out of it, as it also exudes a strong sense of unease. Carving this material is a constant struggle against fear.

Colossal Paw.q: It is said that these paws can suddenly take on a life of their own to crush the skulls of those who cut them off.

Vial.q: A small vial made of glass, used to craft medicines and alchemical items.

src: The Workshop makes 2 per rest when a Tinkerer staffs it.
